declared_legacy_snapshots.reason: The e2e fixture ships a 0.82-era COPY of the engine (≈579KB vs the canonical ≈1.08MB; ~34.7k differing lines). Its routes/attribution still reference tokens that FEAT-038 moved out of the router layer (L3897-3902 doc list, L12476-12499 proxy contract text, L12085/L12092 e2e contract paths), so running `governance-context`/`e2e-check` FROM the fixture cwd FAILs. The active matrix never takes that path (`_e2e_target_cwd_command_matrix` runs status/gate/cleanup only), so there is no live failure. Options weighed at FEAT-040: (a) sync the 4 attribution points by hand — rejected, a 4-line patch on a 34.7k-line divergence manufactures the impression that the copy tracks canonical; (b) promote the file to a byte_copy projection — rejected, a ~530KB fixture rewrite whose blast radius (fixture-local tests and the fixture's own .governance/ assumptions) is far outside a projection-registry task. Chosen: DECLARE the divergence, machine-guarded (this entry, not prose) — `check_legacy_snapshots` reddens if the file disappears, and reddens if it ever converges (a converged copy must be promoted to a real projection instead of keeping a stale 'legacy' label). FIX-380 note (review-FIX-378-CODE-R0 N-1, disclosure completeness): since this entry was written, the copy has received exactly one intentional, documented defect backport — the quote-entry guard at copy L6887 is a FIX-378 targeted backport of the FIX-373 splitter fix (`not in_code_span`-guarded), provenance disclosed in the copy's function docstring (L6857). The rejection narrative above remains the attribution-point decision record; this note adds the backport fact only — no declared field value changes.

legacy_snapshot_backport_policy.decision_basis: arch consultation 2026-09-23 Q4 ruling: declared snapshots + controlled backport beats single-sourcing — the fixture freeze has isolation value (e2e tests stay undisturbed by canonical evolution). Single-sourcing would erase a deliberate isolation boundary; the backport face makes divergence a managed resource instead of an implicit parity debt. The only pre-existing backport instance is FIX-378 (registered on the fixture-engine entry below).

snapshot_inventory.note: the inventory IS the controlled backport surface — this block references it and never duplicates it (one list, one truth); adding a declared snapshot automatically brings it under this policy

trigger.evaluate_when: a defect fix lands in a canonical file that has a declared legacy snapshot copy
criteria_all: same-origin region: the defective code region exists in the snapshot copy (shared lineage, not a look-alike)
live region: the copy region is reachable by fixture execution or fixture tooling — dead code never triggers
real effect: left unpatched, the defect would corrupt fixture behaviour or fixture governance data
dispositions: backport: apply the minimal patch, register it in the snapshot's approved_backports ledger, run the dual_run_contract
not-applicable: record the reasons next to the snapshot entry (precedent: FIX-380 note 3 classified the e2e splitter-pin as not-applicable with four reasons)
trigger.default: evaluate every time — silence is not a disposition

ledger.location_rationale: chosen over a standalone ledger file: check_legacy_snapshots already reads this registry, so ledger validation rides the existing falsifiability machinery with zero new manifest surface; a standalone file would need a second reader for no added property
ledger.guard: check_legacy_snapshots validates required fields and resolves anchor_symbol + marker against the copy text — a ledger entry whose anchor no longer resolves, or whose patch marker is gone, reddens (a stale ledger is a failure, not a memory)
ledger.anchor_convention: anchor_symbol names the function/def the patch touches (line numbers rot — the FIX-388 re-anchor burden is the cautionary precedent); marker is a stable text fragment the patch itself leaves in the copy (provenance docstring)

dual_run_contract.requirement: an approved backport is not closed until the reproducing probe passes in BOTH trees
dual_run_contract.canonical_leg: run the probe against the canonical engine from the repo root
dual_run_contract.snapshot_leg: run the same probe against the snapshot copy (fixture cwd, or the extracted region when a full fixture run is out of scope)
dual_run_contract.parity: both legs must agree on the fixed behaviour; the probe must FAIL on the pre-fix state — a probe that cannot fail proves nothing
dual_run_contract.sample: FIX-378: quote-in-code-span table row (EVD-248 shape, 10 data cells). Canonical leg + snapshot leg both fold-proof after the not in_code_span guard; smoke red->green LIVE 6/5->12/10 (FIX-378 commit record)

checklist: fixture-own tests bound to the copy (the fixture-test-verify-workflow <-> fixture-engine pair): do they encode the fixed behaviour? patch or promote the pair in the same change, never one side alone
registry machinery keyed on the file (PROJECTION_SYNC_PATTERNS members, declared snapshot paths, FIXTURE_PREFIX): a backport must not move declared paths or pattern members

third-copy drift of mirrored DATA, not just code (precedent: FIX-379 found the task_priority prefix vocabulary drifting in archive.py L967-971 — 18 vs the authoritative 20): does the patched region or any table it reads exist in further copies? record a disposition per copy
cross-file contracts the fixture consumes (plan-tracker parsing shape, governance records the fixture writes): output shape must stay fixture-compatible
coupling_check.record: coupling_reviewed field on each ledger entry (per-item disposition or a review-report reference)

replay_path.rule: declared snapshots are frozen — regenerating one from canonical is NOT a supported write; if a copy is ever regenerated (re-pinned at a new generation, or canonical-copied) the approved backports must be replayed or the declaration retired
steps: 1. the whole-file converged guard reddens (expected — do not silence it)
2. re-apply every approved_backports entry onto the fresh copy: anchor_symbol locates the region, the source-fixed region is re-applied, the marker restored
3. re-run the dual_run_contract for each replayed backport
4. update the ledger anchors; divergence must be re-established before the declaration can pass again
replay_path.canonical_regenerated_case: if the fresh copy is byte-identical to canonical the exemption reason is gone entirely: promote to a byte_copy projection, delete the declaration, retire the ledger (the backports are absorbed by canonical tracking)

guard_semantics_review.question: does converged-red misfire after a controlled backport, since the backported region becomes identical to canonical?
guard_semantics_review.conclusion: no misfire: the trigger is WHOLE-FILE byte equality (path bytes == canonical bytes), and a local backport on a genuinely divergent snapshot cannot satisfy it (fixture-engine keeps ~34.7k divergent lines after its one backport). What the review did surface: the converged DISPOSITION text was backport-blind — for a backport-bearing snapshot it now names the two legitimate exits (replay-then-redeclare, or promote-and-retire) instead of a bare promote instruction. Trigger granularity: unchanged.
